title: Engine choice: a lazy `collect()` runs on the streaming engine by default
verdict: `auto` is streaming for lazy queries, in memory for eager ones; four switches change it
description: `collect(engine="auto")`, the default, uses the engine set by `Config.set_engine_affinity` or `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY`, and otherwise the streaming engine (docstring at py-2.1.0). The Rust side resolves `Engine::Auto` to the in-memory engine only for eager operations and to streaming for every lazy query (`polars-lazy/src/frame/mod.rs`); eager `DataFrame` methods always run in memory (`_eager_engine`). With `engine="streaming"` there is no whole-query fallback: `collect_with_engine` runs `polars_stream::run_query` and returns its error. The fallback is per node: the lowering hands operations it cannot stream to the in-memory engine inside the streaming plan (polars-exec-streaming-fallback). The only whole-query switch is `POLARS_AUTO_STREAMING=1`, which tries streaming first for a non-streaming engine.

sverify targets the streaming engine (#605 pins `collect(engine="streaming")`), so the settings that matter are those that move a query off it: `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY` and `Config.set_engine_affinity` no longer apply to an explicit engine, while `POLARS_FORCE_STREAMING` only forces streaming. The risk is the per-node fallback: a node run in memory takes the in-memory engine's algorithms (its float sums, its row order) on a materialized frame. The probes behind polars-sum-float, polars-var-std, polars-cov and polars-mean-float called eager `DataFrame` methods, which run in memory, and need rerunning under `engine="streaming"`.

Switches that change the engine: `Config.set_engine_affinity(name)`, which writes `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY`; `Config.set_engine_affinity(Engine object)`, which clears the variable and keeps the engine in a Python-side override; `POLARS_FORCE_STREAMING=1`, which forces streaming whatever the affinity; `POLARS_AUTO_STREAMING=1`, which tries streaming first for a non-streaming engine. `POLARS_MAX_THREADS`, read once at import, sets the thread pool. `pl.Config`'s other settings change display only.
Next round: probe the engine-dependent facts under `engine="streaming"`, and the result of `collect()` with each switch.
reference: The reference has no engine choice. A profile's facts hold under the settings they record (`sverify._engine_settings`, #444); the Polars row accepts the affinity `auto` and `in-memory`.

evidence.note: Engine::Auto: in memory if eager, else streaming; POLARS_FORCE_STREAMING, POLARS_AUTO_STREAMING
eager operations in memory; an Engine-object override beats the variable
collect calls lf.collect with no engine
collect_with_engine: Streaming runs polars_stream::run_query, no whole-query fallback
InMemoryMap: per-node fallback to the in-memory engine

provenance.notes: Corrects round 1's 'a query the streaming engine cannot run falls back to the in-memory engine': the fallback is per node, inside the streaming plan.
